s1loc: Hoddesdon sits in the Borough of Broxbourne, where Broxbourne Foodbank runs as part of the national Trussell network, taking referrals through a voucher system and leaning on local volunteers for sorting, packing and distribution. Isabel Hospice has a strong retail presence on the high street, with a Hoddesdon shop and a clearance shop selling fashion, homeware and accessories. The Love Hoddesdon partnership pulls together businesses and charities, while the big food-redistribution and foodbank networks keep the town stocked.

The sector runs at every size. National and regional charities such as Isabel Hospice and the Trussell-backed Broxbourne Foodbank operate shops and central buying, while small community groups, church-run pantries and volunteer-led projects work on a shoestring across Rye Park, Hoddesdon town centre and the Borough of Broxbourne. Beyond the foodbank, Isabel Hospice draws hundreds of volunteers across its Hertfordshire shop network, and dedicated retail teams keep the Hoddesdon and clearance stores trading. Hertford and District Foodbank serves households just up the road, and church and community projects around Rye Park and the Lea valley run informal larders and mutual-aid collections. The Salvation Army and parish groups add coffee mornings, clothing banks and befriending rounds, so the volunteer effort spreads well past the single high street into the surrounding Broxbourne neighbourhoods.

Hope Central, a charity covering north east Cheshire, pairs a foodbank with a Debt Centre and Job Club under its relieving-poverty banner. East Cheshire Hospice cares for the wider area, supported by the Wilmslow and District group covering Wilmslow, Handforth and Alderley Edge, while CVS Cheshire East coordinates volunteering across the borough.

The sector runs at every size. The Wilmslow and District Rotary supports local and international causes, Wilmslow Knit and Natter and Wilmslow Girls Crafts for Charity raise funds for The Christie and East Cheshire Hospice, and Wilmslow In Bloom draws together voluntary groups. The East Cheshire Hospice shop in Handforth adds another retail outlet staffed by local volunteers.

grays thurrock.s1_head: Grays Thurrock charity and volunteer life

Thurrock CVS supports the wider voluntary, community and faith sector and runs Volunteer Centre Thurrock from The Beehive Resource Centre on West Street, Grays. A food and hygiene bank works from the same Beehive hub several evenings a week, while the Salvation Army in Grays runs a community kitchen for people facing homelessness and hardship.

The sector runs at every size. We serve the national charity with shops across Grays Thurrock and the one-room foodbank in equal measure, with trade accounts for the larger names and direct online ordering with no minimum for the smallest volunteer groups.

The volunteer base reaches well beyond the foodbank. St Luke's Hospice is opening shops in stages across Thurrock, including Tilbury and Chadwell St Mary, each staffed by local volunteers. Grays Baptist Church runs community activities and groups, and SNAP and other family charities operate from the borough. Volunteer Centre Thurrock at The Beehive places people into formal and informal roles across Grays, from the community kitchen and food bank to befriending and cost-of-living support run by Thurrock Council and partner groups.

The borough's Trussell foodbanks at Collier Row and Romford, Harold Hill and Rainham are partnered by Havering Volunteer Centre, which recruits and places volunteers. new milton.s1_head: New Milton charity and volunteer effort
s1loc: New Milton sits on the edge of the New Forest, where the New Forest Basics Bank provides food and essentials parcels to households in crisis across the district. It runs four weekly community larders, in New Milton, Pennington, Ashley and Bransgore, in partnership with FareShare and local volunteers, with the New Milton and Pennington larders seeing the greatest need. Oakhaven Hospice cares for patients across the New Forest and Waterside and runs a charity shop in New Milton itself.

The sector runs at every size. National and regional charities such as Oakhaven Hospice operate high-street shops and central buying, while small community groups, church larders and volunteer-led projects work on a shoestring across New Milton, Ashley, Barton on Sea and the wider New Forest. We serve the national charity with shops across New Milton and the one-room foodbank in equal measure, with trade accounts for the larger names and direct online ordering with no minimum for the smallest volunteer-run larders and pantries.

The volunteer effort here is striking. New Forest Basics Bank is staffed by close to three hundred unpaid volunteers, with volunteer drivers delivering around four in five parcels across a rural area with thin public transport. Oakhaven, an independent local charity raising the bulk of its multi-million-pound running costs from the community, keeps high-street shops in New Milton, Highcliffe, Lymington, Hythe and Totton, all needing volunteers in every department. Community larders and mutual-aid groups around Barton on Sea and Ashley add further shoestring support.

Home-Start Southport and Formby trains volunteers to support young families at home, and church-run larders, lunch clubs and mutual-aid groups around Freshfield, Crosby and Bootle add shoestring support, giving local people plenty of routes to help beyond the charity-shop counter.
